equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR consolidated BS, Note 5 non-current financial investments Rs 119.82 crore; their income (dividends, FV gains) is stripped from the flows

equity_bridge.item: Investments in associates (PPG-AP, APPPG) at 15x FY2026 share of profit
equity_bridge.note: Share of profit Rs 165.59 crore x 15; book value Rs 656.09 crore (6,561m). Earnings sit below EBITDA so are not in the flows

historical_growth.revenue_10yr_cagr_note: Raw 10-year 9.6% (FY2016 142,715m -> FY2026 355,835m) is understated: FY2016-FY2017 revenue is gross of excise duty (15,702m in FY2016). On an excise-adjusted base the 10-year CAGR is ~10.8%.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income, applied across the history: FY2021 33,341.6m; FY2023 27,858.8m; FY2026 54,108.8m. The 3-year figure is off a working-capital-depressed FY2023 base and onto a working-capital-released FY2026 -- noise, not trend.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: 5-year revenue (10.4%) and equity (10.8%) CAGRs, haircut for the structural share loss to Birla Opus since FY2025; the base 10-year revenue path compounds at ~8.1%, front-loaded by the FY2027 pricing-led +14%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-year equity CAGR 10.1% diverges >30% from 3-year revenue (1.05%) and EPS (1.75%). Equity compounded through retained earnings while revenue and EPS flat-lined through the FY2024-FY2026 Birla Opus disruption and the FY2025 margin trough. The operating CAGRs are the honest 3-year picture; the equity figure is not evidence of operating growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs run ~0.4pp below reported-FCF CAGRs over 5 years: interest income (673m -> 1,809m) has grown faster than FCF as the investment pile built, so a rising slice of reported FCF growth is investment income, not operating cash. SBC is immaterial throughout.

scenario_narratives.base: The disruption is real but bounded. Asian Paints keeps ~50-52% share on distribution depth and brand, grows roughly with the category less a share-loss drag (9% fading to 5.5%), and operating margins recover from the FY2027 raw-material trough to the middle of the guided band -- not to the FY2024 peak. Capex normalises after VAM-VAE Phase 2. Axes: Birla Opus share trajectory; crude/TiO2 pass-through lag; VAM-VAE margin benefit; home-decor losses.
scenario_narratives.bull: Share loss stops at ~52%, the price war eases as Birla Opus turns to profitability, volume returns to 8-10%, premiumisation and waterproofing improve mix, backward integration and cost programmes restore ~20.5% operating margins (near FY2024). Several independent things must go right at once.
scenario_narratives.bear: Birla Opus (and JSW) keep scaling with deep pockets; share and realisations erode structurally; margins settle at second-tier-peer levels; growth drops to mid-single digits; working capital is deployed to defend dealers. No solvency risk -- the company carries ~Rs 5,000 crore net cash -- so the bear case is a franchise-value case, not a going-concern case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on operating cash flows only: company 'EBITDA' is restated to exclude other income, the Rs 7,480 crore investment pile and the PPG associates are added back in the bridge once, leases are charged in the flows, SBC is expensed with a flat share count, and all three scenarios are discounted at one INR WACC with risk carried in the flows and the weights. The base case deliberately does not extrapolate the pre-disruption FY2024 margin or the pre-FY2024 growth rate; the bull case is where those return. The result is compared with a market price that currently capitalises FY2026 earnings at ~55x.
key_risks_to_valuation: Birla Opus share trajectory: each further 1pp of share is ~2% of revenue and more than that of margin through operating deleverage and trade spend
Raw-material pass-through: crude derivatives and TiO2 (with new anti-dumping duties) are ~55% of sales; a 100bp gross-margin miss unpassed is ~5% of base-case value
Terminal assumptions dominate: ~65-70% of EV is terminal; +/-50bp on terminal growth or WACC moves value ~8-10%
Home-decor and international profitability: still loss-making/volatile; the base assumes they do not drag margins below the path
Multiple compression: the market pays a quality premium no 10.8% INR DCF reaches; the valuation is a statement about cash flows, not about where the stock trades next year

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NSE regular close); 52-week range 2,115-2,986
data_sources.financials: ASIANPAINT.NS_Metrics.csv (consolidated, INR millions, FY2016-FY2026 and quarters to Q2 FY2027); FY2026 consolidated annual report (balance sheet, P&L, Notes 5, 24, 26, 28, 29, 37; consolidated cash-flow statement for lease principal/interest and tax paid); Q1 and Q2 FY2027 investor presentations for H1 FY2027 net sales and PBDIT margin
data_sources.qualitative: ASIANPAINT.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): competitive position, Birla Opus disruption, FY2027 guidance (18-20% PBDIT band, 8-10% volume), VAM-VAE capex programme

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares FY2026, consolidated EPS note (95,87,91,026); 959.2m issued less treasury shares held by the ESOP trust. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated annual report, Note 26 employee benefits: share-based payment expense Rs 29.35 crore (FY2025 Rs 21.25 crore). No cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (none in financing activities).
inputs.buyback_note: Rs 30.92 crore of treasury-share purchases by the ESOP trust in FY2026 -- a hedge of ESOP grants, not a capital-return programme. Dividends (Rs 2,402.87 crore paid in FY2026) are the distribution mechanism; the flat share count is funded by the ESOP trust purchases, roughly matching SBC.
inputs.price_note: NSE regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: The company's reported 'EBITDA' (Rs 7,419.72 crore, 20.9%) INCLUDES Other Income of Rs 723.80 crore (interest 180.93, FVTPL gains on investments 286.50, dividends, misc). The driver margin paths are OPERATING EBITDA ex other income: FY2026 = 66,959m = 18.8%. All other income is stripped from the flows and its source assets (73,595m cash/bank/current investments; 1,198m non-current investments) are added in the bridge once -- the matching-asset rule. Management's 18-20% guided band is on the incl-other-income basis; other income runs ~2% of revenue, so that band is ~16-18% on the operating basis used here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: INR-built. India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% (Nov 2026); India equity risk premium ~6.75% (mature-market ERP plus country risk, Damodaran basis); Asian Paints beta ~0.65 (low-beta consumer franchise) -> cost of equity ~10.9%. Borrowings are ~1% of EV (Rs 2,293 crore at ~3.7% after tax), pulling WACC to ~10.8%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: competitive, raw-material and execution risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Consolidated lease cash cost FY2026 = Rs 459.10 crore (principal 339.78 + interest 119.32, consolidated cash flow statement) = 1.29% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (1.3%). Lease liabilities (Rs 1,635.67 crore = 16,357m) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings only (non-current 1,247.17 + current 1,046.09 crore = 22,932.6m). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation: 12,288.5 - 3,924.9 (ROU, Note 29) = 8,363.6m = 2.35% of revenue.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated. NCI (Rs 643.39 crore book; FY2026 NCI profit share Rs 69.34 crore) deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at 15x FY2026 NCI profit (-10,401m), the same multiple applied to the associates. Not folded into the flows.
inputs.associates_treatment: Share of profit in associates (PPG-AP and APPPG industrial-coatings JVs; Rs 165.59 crore FY2026, Rs 140.71 crore FY2025; book Rs 656.09 crore) is below EBITDA and therefore outside the flows. Added in the bridge at 15x FY2026 share of profit (+24,838m, ~Rs 25.9/share) -- a 50%-owned auto/industrial coatings JV with PPG growing ~18% warrants an earnings basis rather than book (Rs 6.8/share).
inputs.tax_note: Statutory 25.17%. FY2026 current tax 1,550 crore on PBT ex-associates 5,838 crore = 26.6%; cash tax paid 1,573.82 crore. Cash rate 26% used throughout -- no carryforwards, no one-offs.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer/distributor: inventories 57,437m + receivables 44,618m exceed payables 38,630m; operating NWC ~12-15% of revenue. Growth consumes cash, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-12% base, -10% bull, -15% bear where dealer credit is extended to defend share). FY2026 reported FCF (56,212m, 15.8% of revenue) carries a ~15bn working-capital release (inventory down 976 crore, payables up) that will not repeat; the component build starts from operating EBITDA, not from that FCF.
inputs.fy27_anchor: H1 FY2027 (to 30 Sep 2026): consolidated net sales Rs 20,475 crore, +17.4% YoY (Q1 +17.9%, Q2 +16.9%), of which ~12% cumulative price increases; consolidated PBDIT margin 18.2% incl other income (Q1 20.6%, Q2 15.6%). Year-1 base growth 14% assumes H2 slows to ~11% as price hikes anniversary; year-1 operating EBITDA margin 16.5% is H1's ~16.4% ex-other-income with a modest H2 recovery as pricing catches up with raw-material inflation.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), the operating-company route in .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md, with the non-US adaptations (INR WACC, single lease treatment, NCI charged once, excluded income matched to its asset in the bridge). Chosen because Asian Paints is a manufacturing/consumer operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; no prior DCF exists for this ticker (fresh build, 2026-11-08). 10-year horizon because the margin is recovering from a trough and capex is normalising from the VAM-VAE build-out -- a 5-year horizon would capitalise an immature year. SBC is immaterial (0.08% of revenue), so house and street bases nearly coincide. Reported FCF history: FY2016-17 revenues are gross of excise duty (pre-GST); 10-year revenue CAGR is overstated on the raw series and the 5-year/3-year figures are the clean ones. Terminal cap multiple 20x does not bind in any scenario (Gordon at 10.8%/5.0% = 18.1x base).

bear.narrative: Structural erosion: Birla Opus keeps taking share (towards 15%+) with Grasim's balance sheet behind it, JSW Paints scales, and the category's realisations stay under pressure; Asian Paints' share slides towards the mid-40s and growth falls to 4-5% nominal. Operating EBITDA compresses to 14.5% (~16.5% incl other income, below the guided band; Berger-like economics) as TiO2 anti-dumping duties and crude-derivative costs cannot be fully passed through. Dealer credit is extended to defend share (-15% WC capture); capex is cut to 3%. Terminal growth 4%.

base.narrative: FY2027 +14% is largely locked by H1 (+17.4%, ~12% pricing); growth then settles at 9% and glides to 5.5% -- roughly industry nominal growth (5-7% volume plus 2-4% price/mix) less a persistent share-loss drag. Operating EBITDA troughs at 16.5% in FY2027 (raw-material inflation flowing through, Q2 15.6% PBDIT) and recovers to 17.5% (~19.5% on the company's incl-other-income basis, mid guided band) -- below FY2026's 18.8% and the FY2024 ~21% peak, because the market now has three scaled national competitors. Capex 4.5% for two years (VAM-VAE Phase 2) then 3.2%. Terminal growth 5% nominal INR.

bull.narrative: Share stabilises at ~52% as Birla Opus's growth normalises and the price war eases; volume growth returns to the 8-10% guided range with premiumisation and waterproofing adding mix; home decor reaches breakeven; international compounds mid-teens. VAM-VAE backward integration (Phase 2 VAM on stream) and cost programmes lift operating EBITDA to 20.5% (~22.5% incl other income, near the FY2024 peak). Higher growth capex (3.4%) and terminal growth 5.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the Birla Opus entry is a structurally different, well-funded competitor whose share gains are two years old and still running, and FY2027 margins are currently printing below the guided band. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs share stabilisation, raw-material relief, backward-integration margin delivery and competitor rationalisation to coincide. Base 50%: the balance sheet (net cash, no refinancing risk) and brand/distribution depth make outright franchise collapse unlikely, so the central case remains a slower, lower-margin compounder.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
